summary: The base accepts the reported NGRAM plus effective torch_native configuration. The exact candidate rejects it with an actionable pre-model-load ValueError and preserves supported controls. The change is Python-only and fully satisfies the original issue's requested validation contract.

tests.what_was_measured: The real base attention compatibility hook accepted NGRAM plus combined torch_native, EAGLE plus torch_native, and NGRAM with either split backend set to torch_native. Supported controls passed. Imports resolved to /job/repo/python.

All four unsupported configurations rejected with the intended ValueError; plain torch_native, NGRAM plus Triton, and a generic torch_native value fully overridden by supported split backends remained valid. Plain torch_native still disabled both CUDA-graph phases.
Candidate regression: 4 tests passed with 2 split-backend subtests.
228 tests and 46 subtests passed. Two unrelated HIP context-parallel tests failed because the prepared ROCm platform rejects deprecated prefill CP before their expected conditions.

gpu_execution.evidence: No model inference or GPU kernel was needed for the pre-model-load validation check. The assigned host is AMD Instinct MI355X gfx950, not the issue's NVIDIA CUDA architecture.

remaining_limitations: No Qwen model weights or NVIDIA GPU were available, so the later full-server warmup crash was not reproduced on the report's architecture.
The validation-path reproduction establishes the original missing rejection but does not claim model semantic accuracy, distributed execution, or multi-node behavior.
The full server-argument test file has two unrelated ROCm context-parallel expectation failures.
No native rebuild was applicable because the candidate changes no native or FlyDSL source.
